sections.h2: Where in Boone is the Watauga County deeds office?
sections.html:
Inside the courthouse, Room 119, at 842 West King Street. Mail goes to the same street, Suite 9, Boone, NC 28607. The county contact page gives 828-265-8052 for land records, 828-265-8034 for vital records and 828-265-7632 for fax.

Watauga County lies in the Blue Ridge Mountains of northwestern North Carolina. It was cut from parts of Ashe, Caldwell, Wilkes and Yancey in 1849 and takes its name from the Watauga River. Boone, the seat, is home to Appalachian State University, and the Blue Ridge Parkway crosses the county.

Voters elect the register, per G.S. 161-1. Wills are filed with the clerk of court, and the county says liens and judgments on real property are checked with the clerk of superior court.

sections.h2: What can be searched in the Watauga County land records?
sections.html:
The website carries indexes and images from 1872 forward, searchable by name or by book and page. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 lives under the old index books tab, because on that date deeds and deeds of trust were folded into one series, the Book of Records, restarting at Book 1.

Plats can be searched by book and page, subdivision, or the owner as grantor, no matter when they were recorded. North Carolina's indexing standards began in 1995, and the office keeps copies.

Nearly everything filed is public. The county names one exception: military discharges on file under 80 years. For the owner of a given parcel, the FAQ sends you to tax mapping at 828-265-8030.

The county's tax mapping department, not the register, answers parcel ownership questions. That split is typical in North Carolina: the register's index runs on names and recorded documents, while tax mapping runs on parcels and maps. Keep both numbers handy when you prepare a sale, and bring the book and page of your deed to either call.

sections.h2: What does the Watauga County fee page list?
sections.html:
The county's schedule, marked as revised October 1, 2016, tracks G.S. 161-10. A deed opens at twenty-six dollars for fifteen pages; a deed of trust opens at sixty-four dollars for thirty-five. Each added page is four dollars in both cases.

Selected lines from the Watauga County register fee page
Line itemAs printed
Deeds and instruments$26.00, then $4.00 a page after 15
Mortgages and deeds of trust$64.00, then $4.00 a page after 35
Records of satisfactionNo fee
Non-standard document$25.00 on top of the filing fee
Parties beyond twenty$2.00 each
Multiple instruments$10.00 per extra instrument
Plats$21.00 a sheet
Excise stamps$1.00 per $500.00 or fraction

A 1983 commissioner ordinance, noted on the page, requires plats offered for registration to measure 18 by 24 inches. Records supplied to help someone claim veterans' benefits are free.

Fees apply per instrument, so a closing that records a deed and a new deed of trust is billed on two lines. Releases of an old loan add nothing. The county page also notes that the schedule is posted for the public to read, so you can compare it with your closing statement.

sections.h2: Does Watauga County accept electronic recording?
sections.html:
Yes, for all land record document types. The county says more than 1,500 submitters, such as banks, law offices and mortgage companies, already send documents this way.

Three vendors are named:

  • Simplifile, 1-800-460-5657.
  • Corporation Service Company, 1-866-652-0111.
  • eRecording Partners Network, 1-888-325-3365.

Most home sales arrive electronically through the lawyer handling the closing, so sellers seldom carry paper in. Deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, easements and powers of attorney are all on the county's list of electronic filings.

sections.h2: What will the Watauga County register's staff not do for a seller?
sections.html:
Staff can point you to the right book and tell you whether a document is a real estate record or a vital record, but the county says they cannot run a title search, offer a legal opinion, or change a deed already recorded. Adding or deleting a name would count as practicing law, so that job goes to an attorney.

Address searches are also off the table. This office indexes documents by legal description, with boundary, lot, block and acreage details, so a street address has to go to the Tax Mapping Department at (828) 265-8030.

  • A lost deed is replaceable: a copy can be certified with the office seal, because the recording matters more than the paper.
  • Copies cost five cents a page, and a recorded subdivision plat copy is one dollar.
  • If no money changes hands, no excise stamp applies.
  • A person with private data in online records can ask in writing, at no charge, for it to be removed from the online copy under the Identity Theft Protection Act of 2005.

The office is open weekdays from 8:00 to 5:00 except holidays, and marriage licenses are by appointment, with applicants in the door by 4:30.

sections.h2: Who covers the excise stamp on a Boone-area deed?
sections.html:
The seller. The stamp is a dollar for each $500 or fraction of the consideration, paid to the register before the instrument is entered. The county gets half and the Department of Revenue gets half, per G.S. 105-228.30.

The settlement statement carries the final amount. North Carolina also repealed its estate tax for deaths on or after January 1, 2013, so an inherited Watauga County house adds no estate tax step before recording.

sections.h2: What else does the Watauga County register's office provide?
sections.html:
Besides land, the fee page lists marriage licenses at $60 and certified birth, death and marriage copies at $10. Notary oaths are $10, with $2 for verifying a commission. Military discharge records are kept, and a certified copy of an armed forces discharge costs nothing.

The county menu also lists an assumed business name certificate, a redaction request form, a fraud notification system and an identity theft page. Because deeds and deeds of trust are public, the fraud notice and the redaction form are the two a homeowner is most likely to use.

  • Uncertified copies cost whatever is posted at the office.
  • Comparing a copy for certification is $5.00.
  • For birth and death certificates, call 828-265-8034.

sections.h2: Must a Watauga County deed be recorded, and can I write my own?
sections.html:
The county says to record soon after drafting, since an unrecorded deed can make a later sale or mortgage impossible to prove. The law backs it up: G.S. 47-18 denies a conveyance force against lien creditors and paying purchasers until it is registered where the land lies.

An owner may write a deed, the county notes, though an attorney is strongly advised. Adding or removing a name takes a new deed, and the register has no blank forms.

A search of the index shows how the present owner took title, which matters when property passed through heirs or a trust.

sections.h2: What if a Watauga County title has loose ends?
sections.html:
Begin with the index. Look up the owner, note the book and page of the last deed, and watch for old deeds of trust with no recorded release. Releases cost nothing to file.

Next, phone the clerk of superior court about liens and judgments and the tax office about the account. A house with flaws can still sell as it is. If you want a cash offer to compare with listing, you can request one on this site.

faqs.q: Where is the Watauga County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: In the courthouse, Room 119, 842 West King Street, Boone. Dial 828-265-8052 for land records and 828-265-8034 for vital records.

faqs.q: How far back do the online land records in Watauga County go?
faqs.a: To 1872. Anything recorded before February 22, 1985 is under the old index books tab.

faqs.q: Does Watauga County charge to file a release of a deed of trust?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee page lists records of satisfaction at no fee.

faqs.q: Does the Watauga County register keep wills?
faqs.a: No. Wills go to the clerk of courts. Separation agreements can come from the register, while divorces are filed with the clerk.

faqs.q: Can a Watauga County deed be recorded online?
faqs.a: Yes, through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company or eRecording Partners Network. Most sellers let the closing lawyer handle it.
